title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 24
summary: Issued at 800 PM MST Fri Oct 02 2026 014 WTPZ43 KNHC 030240 TCDEP3 Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number 24 NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL EP182026 800 PM MST Fri Oct 02 2026 The convective structure of Rachel has remained largely unchanged since the previous advisory. Visible satellite imagery continues to show a cloud-filled eye inside a central dense overcast (CDO), with much of the deeper convection displaced slightly to the west of the center due to moderate northeasterly wind shear. The latest subjective intensity estimate from TAFB is T4.5/77 kt, while objective estimates from UW-CIMSS range from 79 to 94 kt. The initial intensity is lowered slightly to 85 kt for this advisory, blending the subjective and objective estimates. The initial motion is estimated to be 280/4 kt, or slowly westward. This slow westward motion is expected to continue, with a gradual increase in forward speed and a turn toward the west-northwest over the weekend as the ridge begins to weaken. While the track guidance is in fair agreement with this scenario, there is some guidance disagreement regarding the timing of the forward speed early next week.
